A devastating 7.8 magnitude in the Philippines has destroyed Jollibee restaurant

Disturbing footage has surfaced showing a Jollibee restaurant crumbling to the ground as a devastating 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the Philippines.

The offshore earthquake rocked the southern Philippines on Monday, killing at least 32 people, injuring more than 200 others mostly in damaged buildings and sending a 1-meter (3-foot) tsunami into nearby coasts.

Reports online suggest the structure collapsed in General Santos within the Soccsksargen region, Mindanao. The tremor originated in the southern Philippines, hitting at around 11:38 p.m. UTC on Sunday, prompting the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center to issue warnings for numerous nations across the western Pacific.

The PTWC cautioned that hazardous tsunami waves are likely and could affect parts of the Philippines, Indonesia, Palau, Yap, Taiwan, and Papua New Guinea over the following three hours. The organization noted that the soonest expected arrivals would be along coastal areas near the quake's epicenter in the southern Philippines and eastern Indonesia, shortly past midnight UTC.

Reports indicate that Davao, the nation's largest city, might see the first wave arriving as early as 12:08 a.m. Officials warned that the initial waves of a tsunami are usually not the most dangerous and that tsunamis typically consist of several waves. It was reported that three people have been confirmed dead.

They further stressed that the danger from the water could persist for several hours after the initial impact. Authorities in areas that could be affected have been urged to alert residents and implement emergency procedures as needed.

People residing in low-lying coastal regions have been instructed to monitor official alerts and follow directives from local officials and emergency management agencies. The PTWC confirmed it will issue revised guidance within one hour, or sooner if the situation demands.

The German Research Center for Geosciences reported that the earthquake struck at a depth of 6.2 miles. New Zealand's National Emergency Management Agency is similarly assessing the earthquake's potential effects on its territory.

A 7.3 earthquake struck near Mindanao in the southern Philippines around 11:38 p.m. UTC(Image: X)

"If a tsunami has been generated in this location, it is not likely to arrive in New Zealand for at least 10 hours," the organization said. "This National Advisory has been issued following a rapid assessment of preliminary earthquake information.

"The situation may change as more information becomes available. We will provide an update when we have completed a further assessment," the organization added. One website tracking the tsunami threat noted, "There is no tsunami danger for the U.S. West Coast, British Columbia, or Alaska."

There has to be a comprehensive estimate of the damage the country sustained. (Image: @X)

It continued, "Pacific coastal regions outside California, Oregon, Washington, British Columbia, and Alaska should refer to the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center messages at tsunami.gov."

Separate footage spreading across social media captures buildings and power lines swaying across the Philippines as the earthquake rippled throughout the island nation. "Building under construction shakes violently amid the strong earthquake in the Philippines," reads the video caption.
